title: Quest board mod: pin the auto-start gate with a regression test, and count the resolveLocal child in the tick budget
description:
Filed from QCLI-490's round-2 review (opum-workflow:review-assignment attempt 2 at head ff7ef4ae, job-0pedwv6). Both findings are regression-guard gaps, not live defects; QCLI-490 was approved and landed on that round, so they are filed here rather than fixed there. Not under a ruling.

(a) The auto-start gate has no automated test in either direction. Every session in the mod kit sets isInteractive:true with CLAUDECODE unset, and the tests that call $.session.start reset the recorded opens before asserting, so nothing asserts that the pane auto-opens either. A future edit that removed the gate -- or that misnamed the field it reads, which would silently disable the board for every person rather than for the processes it means to gate -- would still pass `bun run check`. The behaviour itself is covered by QCLI-490's real-process proof, so what is missing is the guard.

(b) The per-tick subprocess budget does not count the resolveLocal git child, so the bound of three rests on CALL ORDER rather than on the arithmetic. checkAlerts awaits resolveLocal first and then seeds its budget with what its READS cost; a tick that actually resolved the repository there would spend one git plus two reads plus one task view. That is not reachable on the shipping paths -- session.start resolves before startAlerts, and tool.call resolves before the pane render's check starts -- but the Pane render calls startAlerts ahead of its own resolveLocal, which is the mount shape the kit's stored-alerts test exercises. This is the same class as the round-1 blocker, which was an under-count in this same budget.

The gate code is hooks/register.tsx `const gated = !e.isInteractive || (await $.env.get("CLAUDECODE")) === "1"`; the budget is MAX_TICK_CHILDREN with `let spent = read.length * 2` and the look-up loop under it.

THIRD CRITERION, added 2026-10-12 under DEC-172 (4bk) Ruling A (opum-doc origin/dev 4db9d29, opum-ai/opum-doc#902), which is the Story disposition for QCLI-490's round-2 minor 3: docs/stories/ship-the-quest-board-mod-in-the-opum-quest-plugin.md keeps its "fleet view" acceptance criterion AS WRITTEN and gains a dated note that QCLI-490 retired fleet view under (4bg). Rewriting a met criterion would falsify history, and leaving it bare would read as a live requirement. QCLI-494 is held off the allowlist until this criterion is on quest-cli origin/dev.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An automated regression test pins the auto-start gate in BOTH directions: a session with `isInteractive` false starts nothing, a session with `CLAUDECODE=1` starts nothing, and an interactive session with `CLAUDECODE` unset DOES start -- the third case being what catches a misnamed field, which would silently disable the board for every person.

The per-tick subprocess budget counts the `resolveLocal` git child, so the bound of three holds by arithmetic rather than by call order, including on the Pane render path where `startAlerts` runs ahead of its own `resolveLocal`. Proved BOTH WAYS: with that child left uncounted the same measurement shows a tick over the bound, and with it counted it does not.

docs/stories/ship-the-quest-board-mod-in-the-opum-quest-plugin.md keeps its "fleet view" acceptance criterion AS WRITTEN -- a met criterion is not rewritten, which would falsify history -- and gains a dated note that QCLI-490 retired fleet view under (4bg), so the criterion does not read as a live requirement.

finalSummary:
DEC-172 (4bl). Three criteria.

AC1 -- the gate pinned in BOTH directions, in the mod kit (tests/board.test.tsx). A session with isInteractive false starts nothing and runs no child; a session with CLAUDECODE=1 does the same; and an interactive session with CLAUDECODE unset DOES open the pane and read the repository. The third case is the one that matters: a gate reading the wrong field, or reading it inverted, would start nothing for every PERSON while both gated cases still passed. The kit answers env.get from a record the test changes between cases, because it refuses a second registration of the same hook; each case ends the standing session first, since the gate's unit is one process.

AC2 -- the per-tick subprocess budget now counts the resolveLocal git child. resolveLocalAndReport returns {repo, spent} -- 1 when it ran the git rev-parse, 0 when the name was already known for this root -- and checkAlerts seeds its budget with that plus the cost of its reads, so the bound of three holds by ARITHMETIC rather than by the caller having resolved first; the Pane render starts the check ahead of its own resolveLocal, which is the path the AC names.

PROVED BOTH WAYS, measured in the AC's OWN UNIT (the subprocesses one alerts tick spawns, counted from the mod's own process.run calls on that path): with the child counted, the tick spends 1 (the name) + 2 (its reads) = 3 and CARRIES the departure to the next tick; with it left uncounted the same tick spends four and goes over, looking the departure up -- the test goes red on the carried assertion, receiving "quest task view OCLI-1 --max-notes 1 --json". The measurement moves the session root between the mount and the tick, so the tick's children are its own and not mixed with the render's concurrent resolve. One kit test that reads the first tick's away-summary is updated with it: this fixture's root is its own, so that tick pays the name and reports one update; the departure lands on the next tick, which the test now asserts.

AC3 -- docs/stories/ship-the-quest-board-mod-in-the-opum-quest-plugin.md keeps its "fleet view" acceptance criterion AS WRITTEN and gains a dated note (2026-10-12) that QCLI-490 retired fleet view under DEC-172 (4bg) item 1 (a), naming (4bk) disposition A as the ruling. A met criterion is not rewritten, which would falsify history.

Verified: bun run check exits 0 (1163 CLI tests, the mod suite 45 pass / 0 fail) and lore check exits 0.
